inputs.original_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the long-delayed 2009 agreement looks less like a sudden dispute and more like a pressure tactic in a system that has let negotiations drag on. The federal government’s delay clearly serves someone, while students and university staff are left to bear the cost. Now the union is warning of an indefinite nationwide strike, a threat reached at its 54th National Executive Council meeting. Whether the standoff is ever resolved, the people making these decisions won’t be the ones paying the price.
inputs.modified_text: This “long-delayed” 2009 agreement is being kept in limbo because the stalemate serves the people in power. The one-month ultimatum and threat of an indefinite nationwide strike after SSANU’s 54th National Executive Council meeting look like pressure being applied within a system designed to keep students and university staff paying the price while decision-makers stay insulated. Don’t assume this is just failed negotiation—the delay itself is doing useful work for someone.
